name: Phase Manager
description: Determines the current phase per task type based on training example count and confidence scores. Phase 1→2 transition: when training example count >= phase1_to_phase2 threshold AND a local model is available. Phase 2→3 transition: when rolling correlation >= phase2_to_phase3 threshold over a sustained number of consecutive windows. Phase 3→2 regression: when correlation drops below coaching_trigger. Phase 3→1 emergency: when correlation drops below emergency_threshold, revert to full remote serving. Transitions are logged as audit events. Phase is derived (computed from state), not stored as a discrete flag — emergent from confidence scores. Quality-based phase is separated from effective operational mode; infrastructure degradation (e.g., local model unavailability) is handled by the caller per error handling rules.

types.name: Phase
types.description: Quality-based operational phase derived from confidence metrics. Not an IntEnum — explicit ordering via a 'level' property (REMOTE_ONLY=1, COACHING=2, AUTONOMOUS=3). Phase is emergent from scores, never manually set.

types.name: TrendDirection
types.description: Direction of the rolling correlation trend over consecutive evaluation windows.

types.name: TransitionTrigger
types.description: Structured reason for a phase transition, used in audit events for machine-readable logging.

types.name: PhaseThresholds

fields.name: phase1_to_phase2_example_count
fields.description: Minimum number of training examples required before transitioning from Phase 1 (REMOTE_ONLY) to Phase 2 (COACHING).

fields.name: phase2_to_phase3_correlation
fields.description: Minimum rolling correlation score required for Phase 2→3 transition. Must be in (0.0, 1.0].

fields.name: coaching_trigger
fields.description: Correlation threshold below which Phase 3 regresses to Phase 2 (COACHING). Must be less than phase2_to_phase3_correlation.

fields.name: emergency_threshold
fields.description: Correlation threshold below which Phase 3 or Phase 2 emergency-reverts to Phase 1 (REMOTE_ONLY). Must be less than coaching_trigger.

fields.name: sustained_windows
fields.description: Number of consecutive evaluation windows where rolling correlation must be >= phase2_to_phase3_correlation before Phase 2→3 transition is granted. Expressed as window counts for deterministic testability, not wall-clock time.

fields.name: cooldown_windows
fields.description: Minimum number of evaluation windows that must elapse after a transition before another transition is permitted. Prevents oscillation. 0 disables cooldown.

types.description: Configuration model for phase transition thresholds. Frozen Pydantic model. Has a model_validator enforcing invariant: emergency_threshold < coaching_trigger < phase2_to_phase3_correlation. Loaded from YAML config. Fails fast on invalid ordering at construction time.

types.name: PhaseMetrics

fields.name: task_id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the task type this metrics snapshot pertains to.

fields.name: example_count
fields.description: Total number of training examples accumulated for this task type.

fields.name: rolling_correlation
fields.description: Current rolling correlation score from the quality tracking system's evaluation window. NaN or negative values indicate insufficient data.

fields.name: local_model_available
fields.description: Whether a local fine-tuned model is currently available and ready for inference for this task. Required for Phase 1→2 transition.

fields.name: consecutive_windows_above_threshold
fields.description: Number of consecutive recent evaluation windows where rolling_correlation was >= phase2_to_phase3_correlation threshold. Used for sustained-period check on Phase 2→3 transition.

fields.name: trend_direction
fields.description: Direction of the correlation trend over recent consecutive windows, as determined by the quality tracking system.

types.description: Frozen Pydantic model containing all inputs needed to compute the current quality-based phase for a single task. Pure data — no behavior. Immutable snapshot of current task state at evaluation time.

types.name: PhaseTransition

fields.name: task_id
fields.description: Task type identifier for which the transition occurred.

fields.name: from_phase
fields.description: The phase the task was in prior to this transition.

fields.name: to_phase
fields.description: The phase the task has transitioned to.

fields.name: trigger
fields.description: Structured reason that caused this transition.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the transition was detected. Injected via clock protocol for testability, not computed internally.

fields.name: metrics_snapshot
fields.description: Complete frozen snapshot of the PhaseMetrics at the moment of transition, for full audit traceability.

types.description: Frozen Pydantic model representing an audit event for a phase transition. Serializable to JSON for structured logging. Immutable record of a detected phase change.

types.name: PhaseComputationResult

fields.name: phase
fields.description: The quality-based phase derived from the provided metrics and thresholds.

fields.name: trigger
fields.description: The transition trigger that best describes why this phase was computed. INITIAL_ASSIGNMENT if no prior phase context.

types.description: Result of the pure phase computation. Contains the derived phase and the trigger reason that would apply if this represents a transition from a different phase.

types.name: TaskPhaseState

fields.name: task_id
fields.description: Task type identifier.

fields.name: current_phase
fields.description: The most recently computed phase for this task.

fields.name: windows_since_last_transition
fields.description: Number of evaluation windows that have elapsed since the last phase transition for this task. Used for cooldown enforcement.

fields.name: transition_history
fields.description: Ordered list of all phase transitions for this task, oldest first.

types.description: Per-task mutable state tracked by the PhaseManager for transition detection, cooldown enforcement, and history. Held in a dict keyed by task_id within the PhaseManager.

types.name: PhaseTransitionList
types.description: Ordered list of PhaseTransition audit events.

types.name: EvaluateResult

fields.name: current_phase
fields.description: The derived quality-based phase after evaluation.

fields.name: transition
fields.description: The phase transition event if a transition occurred, or None if the phase did not change.

fields.name: cooldown_active
fields.description: True if a transition was suppressed due to cooldown enforcement. The computed phase would have changed but cooldown prevented it.

types.description: Result of evaluating a task's metrics through the PhaseManager. Contains the current phase and an optional transition event if a phase change was detected.

types.name: OptionalPhaseTransition
types.description: Optional PhaseTransition — present when a transition occurred, None otherwise.

types.name: TaskPhaseStateMap

fields.name: states
fields.description: Mapping of task_id (str) to TaskPhaseState.

types.description: Dictionary-like container mapping task_id strings to their TaskPhaseState. Used for bulk state inspection and serialization.

types.name: Clock

fields.name: now
fields.description: Method signature: () -> str. Returns current time as ISO 8601 string. Represented here as the protocol's callable interface.

types.description: Protocol (structural typing) for a clock dependency. Must provide a now() method returning an ISO 8601 timestamp string. Injected for testability — production uses real clock, tests use a deterministic stub.

functions.name: compute_phase
functions.description: Pure computation core. Derives the quality-based Phase from a frozen PhaseMetrics snapshot and PhaseThresholds configuration. This function is pure, deterministic, stateless, and trivially unit-testable. It does not consider previous phase, cooldown, or transition history — only current metrics vs. thresholds. The caller (PhaseManager.evaluate) handles statefulness. Logic: (1) If rolling_correlation < emergency_threshold → REMOTE_ONLY. (2) If rolling_correlation < coaching_trigger → COACHING (if example_count >= phase1_to_phase2_example_count and local_model_available, else REMOTE_ONLY). (3) If example_count < phase1_to_phase2_example_count or not local_model_available → REMOTE_ONLY. (4) If consecutive_windows_above_threshold >= sustained_windows → AUTONOMOUS. (5) Otherwise → COACHING.

inputs.name: metrics
inputs.description: Frozen snapshot of current task metrics.

error_cases.name: nan_correlation
error_cases.condition: metrics.rolling_correlation is NaN (not a valid number)

error_data.message: rolling_correlation must be a valid float, not NaN. Caller must handle insufficient data before invoking compute_phase.

error_cases.name: invalid_thresholds
error_cases.condition: PhaseThresholds invariant violated: emergency_threshold >= coaching_trigger or coaching_trigger >= phase2_to_phase3_correlation

error_data.message: PhaseThresholds invariant violated: must have emergency_threshold < coaching_trigger < phase2_to_phase3_correlation

preconditions: metrics is a valid frozen PhaseMetrics instance
thresholds is a valid PhaseThresholds instance (invariant emergency_threshold < coaching_trigger < phase2_to_phase3_correlation holds)
metrics.rolling_correlation is not NaN (caller must handle NaN as insufficient data before calling)
postconditions: Returned PhaseComputationResult.phase is one of Phase.REMOTE_ONLY, Phase.COACHING, or Phase.AUTONOMOUS
If metrics.rolling_correlation < thresholds.emergency_threshold then result.phase == Phase.REMOTE_ONLY
If metrics.local_model_available is False then result.phase in {Phase.REMOTE_ONLY, Phase.COACHING} — never AUTONOMOUS without model readiness consideration at coaching level
If metrics.example_count < thresholds.phase1_to_phase2_example_count then result.phase == Phase.REMOTE_ONLY
If result.phase == Phase.AUTONOMOUS then metrics.consecutive_windows_above_threshold >= thresholds.sustained_windows
Result is fully determined by inputs — same inputs always produce same output
Returned trigger accurately describes the dominant reason for the computed phase

functions.name: evaluate
functions.description: Stateful transition detection layer. Takes current PhaseMetrics for a task, computes the quality-based phase via compute_phase(), diffs against the previously recorded phase for that task, enforces optional cooldown/debounce, and emits a PhaseTransition audit event if the phase changed. Updates internal per-task state (TaskPhaseState). If the task_id has not been seen before, it is initialized to REMOTE_ONLY and the first evaluation may produce an INITIAL_ASSIGNMENT transition. The timestamp for any transition event is obtained from the injected Clock protocol.

inputs.name: metrics
inputs.description: Frozen snapshot of current task metrics.

error_data.message: rolling_correlation must not be NaN. Caller must handle insufficient data.

error_cases.name: clock_failure
error_cases.condition: Injected Clock.now() raises an exception or returns invalid ISO 8601 string

error_data.message: Clock dependency failed to provide valid ISO 8601 timestamp.

preconditions: PhaseManager has been initialized with a valid Clock dependency
metrics is a valid frozen PhaseMetrics instance with non-NaN rolling_correlation
thresholds is a valid PhaseThresholds instance passing all validators and model invariants
postconditions: Internal TaskPhaseState for metrics.task_id is updated to reflect the computed phase (unless cooldown suppressed the transition)
If a transition occurred, EvaluateResult.transition is a frozen PhaseTransition with correct from_phase, to_phase, trigger, timestamp, and metrics_snapshot
If no transition occurred, EvaluateResult.transition is None
If cooldown suppressed a transition, EvaluateResult.cooldown_active is True and current_phase reflects the PREVIOUS phase (not the computed one)
windows_since_last_transition is incremented by 1 for the task, or reset to 0 if a transition occurred
The PhaseTransition (if any) is appended to the task's transition_history
side_effects: Updates internal per-task state (TaskPhaseState) including current_phase, windows_since_last_transition, and transition_history

structured_side_effects.description: Updates current_phase, windows_since_last_transition, and appends to transition_history if transition detected.
Logs PhaseTransition as JSON audit event if a transition occurred.

functions.name: get_task_phase
functions.description: Returns the current quality-based phase for a given task. If the task_id has never been evaluated, returns Phase.REMOTE_ONLY (the default initial phase). This is a read-only query — no state mutation, no transition detection.

inputs.name: task_id
inputs.description: Unique identifier for the task type to query.

error_data.message: task_id must be a non-empty string.

postconditions: If task_id has been previously evaluated, returns the most recently computed phase for that task
If task_id has never been evaluated, returns Phase.REMOTE_ONLY
No internal state is mutated

functions.name: get_task_state
functions.description: Returns the full TaskPhaseState for a given task, including current phase, windows since last transition, and complete transition history. Returns None if the task_id has never been evaluated. Useful for debugging, auditing, and exposing state to the ConfidenceSnapshot builder.

inputs.name: task_id
inputs.description: Unique identifier for the task type to query.

error_data.message: task_id must be a non-empty string.

postconditions: If task_id has been previously evaluated, returns the full TaskPhaseState
If task_id has never been evaluated, returns None
No internal state is mutated

functions.name: get_transition_history
functions.description: Returns the complete ordered list of PhaseTransition audit events for a given task. Returns an empty list if the task has never transitioned or has never been evaluated. Useful for audit trail inspection and debugging.

inputs.name: task_id
inputs.description: Unique identifier for the task type to query.

error_data.message: task_id must be a non-empty string.

postconditions: Returned list is ordered chronologically, oldest transition first
If task_id has never been evaluated, returns an empty list
No internal state is mutated

functions.name: reset_task
functions.description: Removes all tracked state for a given task_id, including current phase, cooldown counters, and transition history. After reset, the task will be treated as never-evaluated on the next call to evaluate(). Logs a structured audit event recording the reset. Returns True if the task existed and was reset, False if the task_id was not tracked.

inputs.name: task_id
inputs.description: Unique identifier for the task type to reset.

error_data.message: task_id must be a non-empty string.

postconditions: If task_id was tracked, all state for that task is removed and True is returned
If task_id was not tracked, no state is modified and False is returned
After reset, get_task_phase(task_id) returns Phase.REMOTE_ONLY
After reset, get_task_state(task_id) returns None
After reset, get_transition_history(task_id) returns an empty list

structured_side_effects.description: Removes all tracked state for the task.
Logs a task reset event as JSON audit record.

functions.name: validate_thresholds
functions.description: Validates a PhaseThresholds instance, checking both individual field constraints and the cross-field invariant (emergency_threshold < coaching_trigger < phase2_to_phase3_correlation). Intended for use at config load time to fail fast on invalid configuration. Returns the validated PhaseThresholds if valid; raises on any violation. This is a static/standalone function, not requiring PhaseManager state.

error_data.message: PhaseThresholds invariant violated: must have emergency_threshold < coaching_trigger < phase2_to_phase3_correlation. Got emergency_threshold={emergency_threshold}, coaching_trigger={coaching_trigger}, phase2_to_phase3_correlation={phase2_to_phase3_correlation}

postconditions: If returned without error, the PhaseThresholds instance satisfies: emergency_threshold < coaching_trigger < phase2_to_phase3_correlation
If returned without error, all individual field validators pass
The returned PhaseThresholds is the same instance as the input (passthrough on success)

invariants: Phase is always derived from metrics, never stored as a manually-set flag — it is emergent from confidence scores
PhaseThresholds invariant: emergency_threshold < coaching_trigger < phase2_to_phase3_correlation — enforced at construction and validated at config load
Phase.REMOTE_ONLY is the universal default — any unknown task, any initialization, any emergency scenario reverts to REMOTE_ONLY
Phase transitions are always logged as structured JSON audit events via the logging side effect
Cooldown enforcement may suppress a transition but never alters the computed phase — it only delays the state update
compute_phase is a pure function: same PhaseMetrics + PhaseThresholds inputs always produce the same PhaseComputationResult output
Phase 2→3 transition requires consecutive_windows_above_threshold >= sustained_windows — sustained period is measured in window counts, not wall-clock time
Phase 1→2 transition requires BOTH sufficient example_count AND local_model_available — either condition alone is insufficient
Emergency revert (→ Phase 1) can occur from any phase when correlation drops below emergency_threshold
No global state — all state flows through explicit parameters, injected dependencies (Clock), or per-task state dictionaries within the PhaseManager instance
Timestamps in PhaseTransition events are always obtained from the injected Clock protocol, never from system clock directly, ensuring testability
Quality-based Phase is separated from effective operational mode — Phase Manager computes quality phase only; infrastructure degradation (local model down, budget exhausted) is handled by the caller
